sections.h2: Picking a route out of a Deerfield Beach house
sections.html:
Choose a route first, then collect what any buyer will ask for: the deed, permit records, the latest tax bill and association paperwork. Cash purchases tend to close soonest, since no lender underwriting sits between signature and closing.

Deerfield Beach is a coastal city in Broward County, and its strategic plan describes housing that ranges from beachfront properties and upscale communities to affordable, family-friendly neighborhoods. Your sale may involve a condo board, an HOA or neither, and that shapes the timeline more than most things.

  • Agent listing: the broadest reach, with showings and financed buyers.
  • Do-it-yourself sale: you run the contract, disclosures and closing.
  • Cash offer: the house goes as-is, which fits inherited, empty, rented or run-down properties.

Deerfield Beach became a city on June 11, 1925. Its 2023 strategic plan lists a land area of 16.22 square miles and a population of 87,414, plus a 5,700-foot public beach and 1,377.68 acres of parks and open space.

The plan sets out priorities that may matter near your property: redevelopment of the City Hall and downtown campus and of central areas, an update of the Comprehensive Plan and the Land Development Code, and a development agreement for 1045 SW 11 Way. In the plan's resident survey of 206 respondents, 63% said the city is improving as a place to live. If your street is close to a redevelopment area, ask city planning staff for the current status before a buyer asks you.

Florida Building Code permits run through an online system, and new applications and plans have gone in electronically since December 15, 2025. The Building Division is at 150 NE 2nd Avenue, open 7:30 am to 4:30 pm, phone 954-250-4060.

  • Inspections are requested online, and a request in by 3:00 PM gets next-business-day service.
  • Every residential permit needs an HOA affidavit.
  • Permit payments over $10,000 are made in person at the city cashier.
  • Online card or bank payments carry a separate transaction fee.

Condo owners get a specific warning on the city's page: the building code does not let a condo owner do the work personally. A permit and a contractor with the proper state credentials are required for items such as water heaters, air conditioner replacements, kitchen and bathroom renovations, windows and doors, hurricane shutters and balcony enclosures. The page adds that hiring an unlicensed contractor is a felony under section 489.127(1)(f).

Unpermitted work on a condo can resurface in an inspection or an insurance review. Collect permits and final inspection records before you list.

A vacation rental is allowed only with registration. Section 98-106 of the Land Development Code makes it unlawful to operate one without it, and registration must be renewed every year by October 1.

Deerfield Beach vacation rental registration terms
RequirementTerm
Renewal dateAnnually, by October 1
Changes to registration detailsReport within 30 days
InspectionsAllowed on reasonable notice
First-offense fineUp to $250 per day
Repeat-offense fineUp to $500

Registrants confirm that every city, county and state registration is current, attach the business tax receipt and confirm that the Deerfield Beach address is the one used for casualty insurance. If the house you are selling was used this way, make sure the registration is current, because a lapse can affect what the buyer is allowed to do with the property.

sections.h2: How the Broward tax bill reaches an owner
sections.html:
Broward County sets values and mails the bill. Value is fixed on January 1, a notice of proposed taxes lands in August, and the bill itself arrives in November.

Exemption applications are due March 1. Homestead reaches $50,000, and the first $25,000 also counts against school taxes. Discounts for early payment slide from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February, and April 1 starts delinquency.

A sale ends the Save Our Homes limit on yearly increases, so the buyer is assessed at just value from the next January 1. If you are moving within Florida, you may be able to carry some of your savings to a new homestead set up within the portability window.

The clerk records the deed and collects documentary stamp tax under section 201.02. Under the revenue department's rules every party is liable, so your contract decides who pays.

Recording charges follow section 28.24 and are billed per page. Spousal homestead deeds and divorce deeds for the marital home have listed exemptions, so ask your title agent whether either fits.

A taxable deed is also a change of ownership. Even a quitclaim to a relative resets the property to just value, unless an exception such as a spousal transfer applies.

No one can sign a deed for an inherited house until the court grants authority. A shortened process called summary administration fits estates under a $150,000 non-exempt ceiling or a death more than two years back, and creditor claims close on a schedule tied to publication or service.

Once a lender has sued, the judgment sets a sale a few weeks out and the top bidder puts down 5 percent. A seller who closes first can repay the loan and keep any surplus.

With a tenant in place, unpaid rent calls for a three-day written notice, and a monthly tenancy ends on 30 days' notice. After judgment, only the sheriff carries out removal.

Start a folder for the deed, the latest tax bill, permit and final inspection records, your insurance declarations and any HOA or condo documents with a current balance statement. Photograph the roof, kitchen, bathrooms and mechanical systems, and write down the dates of repairs. When offers come in, compare the net amount, the time to close and the chance the buyer backs out, and ask each buyer in writing who pays for title and recording.

On closing day, bring photo ID and keys. The title company will show you the settlement statement, and your lender is repaid from the proceeds before the balance is sent to you. Keep copies of everything you sign.

Before any showing, clear the clutter and fix the small things a buyer will notice first, like dripping faucets and sticking doors. If a buyer's inspector turns up a problem, you can fix it, adjust the price or walk away, so think ahead about which of those you would choose. A written list of repairs you have already made helps the conversation stay factual, and it gives your title agent and any lender a clear picture of the house as it stands today.

faqs.q: Does condo work in Deerfield Beach need a permit?
faqs.a: For most work, yes. The city names water heaters, air conditioner replacement, windows and balcony enclosures as permit items needing a contractor with the right state credentials, and it lists interior painting and new floor coverings as exceptions.

faqs.q: How do I submit a Deerfield Beach permit application?
faqs.a: Online, since December 15, 2025, with in-person applications still accepted at the Building Division in City Hall. Call 954-250-4060 for help.

faqs.q: What fines apply to unregistered vacation rentals in Deerfield Beach?
faqs.a: The city's renewal affidavit lists fines up to $250 per day for a first offense and $500 for repeat offenses, and registration can be revoked.

faqs.q: When are Broward property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1, so settle any balance before or at closing.

faqs.q: What does recording a Deerfield Beach deed involve?
faqs.a: The state taxes the consideration under section 201.02, and clerk recording charges are billed by the page under section 28.24.
